history.headline: Yermo Ediciones publishes 'Muerte blanca' by Kid Toussaint and Iñaki Holgado inspired by real soldiers
history.summary: Yermo Ediciones released 'Muerte blanca', a war comic by Kid Toussaint and Iñaki Holgado, inspired by sniper Simo Häyhä and soldier Hiro Onoda. The story follows Riku, shaped by family trauma and war, evolving into a legendary sniper known as the White Death.

history.headline: Marvel replaces Marvel Unlimited with new Marvel Comics App developed with Webtoon
history.summary: Marvel is shutting down the Marvel Unlimited app, replacing it with a new Marvel Comics App co-created with Webtoon. The new app launches November 16, with Marvel Unlimited ending December 7. Registered users can import prior purchases. The new subscription will offer new comics one month after release, improving on Unlimited's three-month delay.

history.headline: Neon Ichiban 3.0 update adds in-app purchasing and Mac desktop digital collection support
history.summary: Neon Ichiban has launched version 3.0 of its app, re-enabling in-app purchasing on Apple and Android, easing comic buying. The update also expands its Mac desktop beta to allow importing DRM-free comics from various sources into a central digital collection, addressing digital ownership fragmentation.

history.headline: DC Studios co-heads Gunn and Safran to report directly to Skydance CEOs
history.summary: In the Skydance/WarnerMount merger, DC Studios co-heads James Gunn and Peter Safran remain in charge and will report directly to Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz. This maintains their previous reporting arrangement under Warner Bros. Discovery. DC's prominent positioning in the corporate branding suggests a strong strategic importance in the new group, underscoring continued investment and focus on DC properties.

history.headline: French comics criticism magazines Bananas and Papiers nickelés maintain strong editorial presence despite distribution challenges
history.summary: Bananas, an annual critical comics magazine led by Évariste Blanchet, plans an autumn release with a varied rich editorial lineup including notable interviews and heritage discussions. Papiers nickelés, a quarterly directed by Yves Frémion, continues to publish insightful articles, including retrospectives on historical artists. However, Bananas faces distribution setbacks following the liquidation of the key distributor Makassar and now relies on direct orders for survival.

08-10-2026 / Comics business and platforms

01 / Industry

French comics criticism magazines Bananas and Papiers nickelés maintain strong editorial presence despite distribution challenges

Bananas, an annual critical comics magazine led by Évariste Blanchet, plans an autumn release with a varied rich editorial lineup including notable interviews and heritage discussions. Papiers nickelés, a quarterly directed by Yves Frémion, continues to publish insightful articles, including retrospectives on historical artists. However, Bananas faces distribution setbacks following the liquidation of the key distributor Makassar and now relies on direct orders for survival.

Why it matters to Komotic: The survival and continued quality of specialist critical comics publications shows enduring interest in heritage and critical discourse despite press sector difficulties. Direct-to-reader sales for Bananas illustrate how smaller publishers adapt but also reveal fragility in traditional distribution, a risk to magazine visibility and influence in the market.

payload.subject: Daily Komotic Briefing | 09-10-2026
payload.html:
KOMOTIC / INDUSTRY INTELLIGENCE

Daily briefing

09-10-2026 / Comics business and platforms

01 / Competition

DC Comics announces new Black Label and Vertigo series at NYCC 2026

At New York Comic Con 2026, DC revealed multiple Black Label one-shots and miniseries. Highlights include 'Green Lantern: The Dying of the Light' by Jason Aaron and Tirso Cons, a gritty Hal Jordan story, and 'Joker/Harley: Malicious Intent.' Vertigo will publish 'Hide Nor Hair' by Adam Smith and Bob Quinn and material like 'Dreambound' transitioning from Webtoon to print. Established titles like '100 Bullets: Enemigos' and 'The Crying Doll' will continue publication in 2027.

Why it matters to Komotic: DC is expanding mature-audience offerings with high-profile creators and storylines, deepening its Black Label and Vertigo lines. This reflects a strategy targeting niche, legacy comic fans and adult readers, possibly drawing market share from smaller imprints and digital-first platforms. Komotic should monitor Black Label's reception for insights into mature content demand.

Zona Negativa | 08-10-2026 | Public text extracted

02 / Industry / Material update

French comics magazines Bananas and Papiers nickelés continue strong editorial output despite distribution loss

The annual comics criticism magazine Bananas, edited by Évariste Blanchet, will publish its autumn edition with a diverse lineup including interviews and historical retrospectives. The quarterly Papiers nickelés continues its work on comics heritage with articles on artists and genres. Bananas suffers distribution challenges after the liquidation of its main distributor Makassar and now relies on direct sales from the publisher for survival.

Why it matters to Komotic: Specialist print publications still engage committed comics audiences despite market pressures and distributor failures. This highlights the fragility of niche comics media infrastructure in Europe. Komotic should keep an eye on how specialist publications adapt and survive, which may indicate broader changes in comics journalism and promotion channels.
